Escape's AI tool for holiday planning just got an upgrade. 

We've listened to user feedback over the first half of 2026 and have re-launched Ask Skye with a slew of new features. 

Before we get into what's new, let's catch you up on what Ask Skye is. 

What is Ask Skye?

Ask Skye is escape.com.au’s next gen AI tool. Its aim? To help you plan the best holiday you’ve ever had.

Where do I find Ask Skye?

Ask Skye is on the homepage of escape.com.au and on articles throughout the site. 

How does Skye work? 

By marrying escape.com.au’s vast array of travel content and expertise with up to the minute pricing information, it can tailor a holiday to your specific interests, destinations, budget, choice of activities, travelling style, travel group and more.

What can Ask Skye do?

It saves you hours on planning as everything is in the one place. It is also super easy to change and refine your itinerary and you can share your personalised plans as a downloadable PDF. This means it’s super easy to share with your family, friends and travel agent. By taking into account your interests and holiday style it helps you discover hidden gems and uncover new favourites.

Ask Skye's new features

1. Group chat - Real-time collaborative planning allowing co-travellers to view, comment on, and edit itineraries together.

2. Ideas - Travellers can now windowshop ideas related to a destination, shortlist them, and add them to their itinerary.

3. Add to calendar - Travellers can now add their trips to their calendar and download an ics file of their itinerary.

4. Destination guides - Ask Skye will now also show travel guides for each destination built from Escape's expert travel content and travel writers.

5. Itinerary generation - Ask Skye instantly converts any existing inspiration (YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, screenshots, blogs, PDFs, photos) into an interactive, customised itinerary. It can either create an itinerary based on the content or create a list of places mentioned in the content.

How to use Ask Skye?

Step 1

It starts with a question. In my case, the brief: “Create me an itinerary for a trip to Bali for two people in September.” This prompts a seven day itinerary with each day mapped out. Day one is a "beachy arrival in Seminyak" including details on suggested transfers, accommodation and a nightcap spot.  Day two is "Canggu Cafes plus beach club day," day three is "move to Ubud: rice fields and wellness" and so on.

After day seven's suggestions it gives me accommodation advice, recommending I split my stay so that I'm in Seminyak for three nights and Ubud for four. It also gives me a rundown on possible hotels, asking me follow up questions on what vibe I'm looking for ("If you tell me your preferred vibe (luxury resort vs boutique vs villa) and an approximate nightly budget in AUD, I can narrow these down to the best-value option and suggest a couple of alternates in the same areas" it asks).

Step 2

Ask Skye then generates a broad itinerary. It includes suggested hotels, restaurants and must-do activities, which I can add to (or delete).

Step 3

This part's smart. Before booking you can share the itinerary with your travel companions who can make changes (which you will get updates on) before you all review, download and book your trip.

Step 4

I could have easily left it there, but I’d forgotten that I wanted to intersperse the eating with a shopping spree or two and Ask Skye hooked me up with a string of bougie boutiques, vintage emporiums and local labels I’d never have heard of otherwise. It also proved helpful in separating the best day spas from the rest.
